# Open In External Browser

**Source:** https://open.seatalk.io/docs/web-sdk_open-in-external-browser

This capability is used for Web SDK on desktop and opens URLs in the system's external default browser.

## Support

| App Capability | Android | IOS | PC |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Web | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

## Parameters

### Input(Object object)

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| url | string | yes | - | Full URL to open in the system/external browser (e.g. https://example.com) |
| onSuccess | function | no | - | Callback function called when the URL is successfully opened |
| onCancel | function | no | - | Callback function called when the user cancels the operation |
| onError | function | no | - | Callback function called when an error occurs |

### Output

None.

## Behavior

### Whitelisted URL vs Non-Whitelisted URLs

To add a domain to the whitelist, configure it in the App Settings page.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

This is how the difference between Whitelisted URL vs Non-Whitelisted URLs:

| URL Type | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Whitelisted URL | URL opens directly in the external browser without a confirmation dialog. |
| Non-Whitelisted URL | A confirmation dialog is shown before opening the URL. The user can choose to proceed or cancel. |

### When is onCancel called

`onCancel` callback is triggered when a user is presented with the confirmation dialog (for non-whitelisted URLs) and chooses to cancel opening the URL in the external browser.
&nbsp;

### How to open a URL in-app

To open a URL within the app's webview instead of the external browser, simply use a standard HTML anchor tag

`Open in-app (https://example.com)`

&nbsp;

## Example

```
import { openInExternalBrowser } from '@seatalk/web-app-sdk';

openInExternalBrowser({
url: 'https://example.com',
onSuccess: () => {
console.log('URL opened successfully');
},
onCancel: () => {
console.log('User cancelled the operation');
},
onError: (err) => {
console.log('Error:', err);
},
});
```
